- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, then decay too slowly — suggesting lag in recognizing downward momentum.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated: model fails to anticipate sharp drops after recent spikes.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, particularly in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Model reacts too aggressively to recent highs, overreacting to short-term volatility.
- Underestimates downward corrections after spikes — often misses the “rebound” phase.
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the middle of the horizon, then drop too abruptly — suggesting poor smoothing of trend changes.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns in the 30-day window — e.g., recurring drops after high peaks.
